//: What a character can do to doors, windows, lamps and lockers (16 §3). Each is content: the engine knows no opening and no switch. `self` is whoever does it, `target` the element, `here` its cell. `if` is tested when it is attempted; a menu lists it greyed out, with `fail_text`, while it does not hold. Bumping into a thing does its `default` one.
name: Open

//: Nobody may stand in what is being shut.
name: Close

//: On and off, for anything with those two states: the lamp of `lighting.json`.
name: Switch

//: Smashes the thing out of the way: it is destroyed as by a blow, and leaves its rubble.
name: Break through

//: Climbs into a thing that holds people: the element becomes its device, and whoever hides is inside it, out of the world until they come out. Only for someone who is not inside something already.
name: Hide inside
fail_text: There is no getting in there now.

//: Searches a thing a person could hide in (a wardrobe, a locker): opens it if it is shut and feels about inside, so that whoever hides there is found, brought out into its cell, in the open. In the dark that is all the searcher has: what it then sees of them is perception's (decision D-950). What the strangers of the last stand do (`core:search_hiding_places`); a player may do it too.
name: Search

//: Comes out of what one hid in, into its cell.
name: Get out

//: Puts whatever one holds in one's hands inside an open thing that holds things: one that opens must be open; a rack, a bench or a stall has no door to open.
name: Put in
fail_text: It must be open, and you must have something in hand.

//: Takes into one's hands what an open thing holds, as much as one's hands take: once they are full the rest is left where it is. What generation left in it is made first, if nobody has looked in it yet (06 §9.3).
name: Take out
fail_text: There is nothing to take, or it is shut.

//: A steel locker: a cell of the grid until someone opens it, puts something in it or hides in it, when it becomes a device that holds them.
name: locker
